children: Australian banks face a tough business environment over the next year as loan growth dries up. Credit growth has held up so far in the face of four interest rate increases, but support is fading, says BMI in a report on the sector. The slowdown should show up first and most strongly in mortgage lending, it adds. Loans settling in mid-2026 largely reflect applications and preapprovals from earlier in the year, before most of the tightening had taken effect, so the slowdown in new lending has yet to feed fully into the headline figure, BMI adds.
